transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Noah (Redwood SE), Rajiv (Cedar Health), Sofia (Cedar IT), Ethan (Cedar Security), Maya G. (Cedar DevOps)

[00:00] Maya (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick check — agenda is networking updates, routing/failover test planning, upgrade notes from the runtime team, and then action items. Anything else to add?
[00:18] Rajiv: No, that's good. Want to make sure we block the maintenance window tomorrow for the routing test. Also to confirm, the pilot is on VPC peering, not transit gateway, right?
[00:30] Liam (SE): Correct, we're using VPC peering for this POC. We have the peering script that was shared last week but there were a couple CIDR overlaps in the customer's initial config so we asked for updated ranges.
[00:45] Sofia: Yeah we updated the ranges, sent them last night but not sure if Liam got them.
[00:50] Liam: I see the e-mail, thanks — will validate the routes after the call.
[01:05] Noah (SE): Quick note — when we run the routing failover test, we'll do a three-step: 1) baseline metrics with primary route, 2) cut to secondary for 10 minutes, 3) revert and validate cache warmup. That'll show cold start impact and any increased token latency.
[01:28] Rajiv: OK good, we're mainly worried about the KV cache and how long warmup takes — we saw spikes last week when the instance restarted during the canary.
[01:40] Liam: Right, last week's canary triggered a restart because of the build mismatch; runtime v2.3.1 rolled back to v2.2 during the incident. We patched the image to prevent automatic restarts but there is still a cache eviction where the KV cache empties and inflight requests see higher p99.
[01:58] Ethan: Can you repeat that — v2.3.1 caused restarts? That's concerning for our compliance team.
[02:05] Maya (AE): Yes — SEs fixed the immediate issue but we'll outline the upgrade plan. The runtime team recommends a rolling upgrade with a staggered drain to keep a fraction of nodes warm, but that requires a short maintenance window.
[02:25] Rajiv: What's the expected downtime per shard? We need an estimate to feed back to ops.
[02:30] Liam: Per node drain is about 60-90 seconds of no-serving while it drains; actual increased latency for in-flight requests depends on cache hit rate — worst case we saw up to +400ms p99 during warmup on previous test. Typical is +120ms after warmup settles.
[02:50] Sofia: Does that +400ms include prefix/KV cache misses? I thought KV cache would localize.
[02:58] Noah: The transcription might say 'KV cash' — but yes, it's KV cache. Cold start means the KV entries aren't warmed, so the runtime has to recompute. If you have a persistent LRU cache and sticky routing, it's minimal. We're recommending sticky routing to the same shard for session-heavy workloads.
[03:20] Rajiv: Sticky routing — we tried it and saw better p50 but p99 still problematic if any node cycles. Any suggestions?
[03:30] Liam: We suggest a hybrid: 85% sticky routing, 15% random for repro/QA. Also enabling prefix caching for common prompts.
[03:40] Sofia: About the network peering — do we need specific SG rules? We use strict egress rules for pods.
[03:46] Liam: We'll share a minimal SG/ACL list. For peering, it's mostly allowing the control plane subnets and port ranges 1024-65535 for ephemeral, plus the healthcheck ports we listed in the doc. I'll attach that.
[04:05] Ethan: On the security side, we're still waiting on KMS integration details. Does Redwood support customer-managed keys via HSM?
[04:15] Maya (AE): Yes, Redwood Private supports both bring-your-own KMS and HSM-backed keys for encryption at rest. There's a small config step in the private control plane — we'll send the step-by-step.
[04:30] Rajiv: Also we need audit logs to show model version changes and who triggered rollouts — that's a compliance requirement.
[04:36] Noah: Audit logging is enabled in the private control plane; we can show you an example export. It includes model version, user id, timestamp, and policy changed.
[04:50] Sofia: Good. Can you also include an example of the console change diff? Our auditors like diffs.
[04:58] Maya G. (DevOps): Quick question — the last upgrade you did, did it require reingestion of the prefix sets? We saw some duplicate tokens in logs which we suspect came from the ingestion job running twice.
[05:12] Liam: There was a race in our ingestion orchestrator that caused duplicate prefix pushes if a node restarted during ingestion. We've added a simple dedupe id in the job; will be fixed in next patch.
[05:25] Rajiv: OK cool. On the routing failover test — can we schedule it for Tue 7/14 02:00-04:00 PDT? That's our maintenance window.
[05:34] Sofia: Yes that works. We'll have network folks on call.
[05:39] Maya (AE): Great — we'll prepare a runbook and list expected metrics to capture.
[05:45] Liam: For benchmarks, I'm going to run a 1,000 request test with mixed prompt sizes: 16% long-form, 70% short, 14% embeddings. I'll share the results and raw logs. That should show cost per token and latency distribution.
[06:05] Rajiv: When can we expect that?
[06:07] Liam: I'll run it tomorrow and post by 7/13 EOD.
[06:12] Ethan: One more security thing — KMS key rotation. Do you have recommendations for rotation frequency and how rotation impacts current sessions?
[06:22] Noah: Rotations are seamless if you follow our key aliasing pattern. A short window of re-encryption may occur but we recommend rotating at low-traffic windows and testing with a copy key in staging. We'll send docs.
[06:38] Rajiv: Any known issues with our cloud provider's VPC limits? We have some soft limits for peering connections.
[06:44] Liam: We noted that as a potential blocker if you have more than 5 peers; we're using a single peering for the POC so should be fine. If you scale to multiple regions we'd discuss transit gateway.
[06:58] Sofia: Good. Regarding cost — we need a rough estimate for delta between hosted and private for our projected traffic (2M tokens/day).
[07:08] Maya (AE): We estimated privately-hosted delta in the last deck. In short, private has higher baseline infra but lower per-token if you run sustained throughput due to reserved instances. I'll resend the cost sheet with updated numbers for 2M tokens/day.
[07:25] Rajiv: Please highlight quantization/instance types; our finance team will ask.
[07:30] Maya: Will do.
[07:35] Liam: Back to the upgrade — there's an optional kernel-level optimization that reduces p99 by ~80ms but requires a quick kernel module preload; it's low risk but we need permission to enable it in the pilot.
[07:48] Ethan: Any security implications?
[07:50] Liam: No, it's purely runtime fast-path; we'll document and run in staging first.
[07:56] Rajiv: Ok we approve doing it in staging; don't enable in prod until after the failover test.
[08:05] Maya G.: For the VPC peering step, we'll need the exact CIDR ranges and the BGP metadata? We don't run BGP on this setup.
[08:14] Liam: No BGP required — simple peering. I'll provide CIDR and ACL ranges.
[08:22] Maya (AE): Quick recap for action items: Maya to send SOC2/security + network doc; Liam to run benchmarks; customer to confirm maintenance window and provide KMS contact. Anything missing?
[08:33] Rajiv: Please also include a short runbook for the failover test with rollback steps.
[08:38] Noah: We'll add rollback steps and expected metrics thresholds.
[08:45] Sofia: One last ask — can you show sample audit log entries for a model rollback?
[08:50] Noah: Yes, we'll attach a snippet.
[08:55] Maya (AE): Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule.
[09:00] [call end]

Transcription notes: occasional mis-words (Redwood Privet, KV cash) and minor punctuation errors. Some speaker overlap and generic Speaker 1 tags where connection blipped.
